sources.entry: LinuxGSM - CLI tool for deployment and management of dedicated game servers on Linux: more than 120 games are supported. (Source Code) MIT Shell

summary.one_liner: LinuxGSM is a command-line tool for quickly deploying and managing dedicated game servers on Linux.
summary.what_it_does: LinuxGSM is a shell-based command-line tool for installing and managing Linux dedicated game servers. The README lists its main features as an installer, monitor, alerts, updater, server details, backup, and console. It states that it supports 100+ game servers, while the awesome-selfhosted listing says more than 120. The README names Ubuntu, Debian, and CentOS as tested distros and says other distros are likely to work but are not fully tested. Each game server has its own dependency requirements, which the README says are listed on the LinuxGSM website. Documentation is at linuxgsm.com and docs.linuxgsm.com.
use_cases: deploy a dedicated game server on linux
manage multiple game servers from the command line
monitor game server status and send alerts
run game servers on ubuntu, debian, or centos
how_to_run: Check the game server's dependency requirements on the LinuxGSM website before installing
notable: Single command-line tool covering install, monitor, alerts, update, backup, and console for many game servers
Supports 100+ game servers according to the README (120+ per the awesome-selfhosted listing)
Has been developed since 2012 according to the README
caveats: Only Ubuntu, Debian, and CentOS are named as tested; other distros are not fully tested
Each game server has its own dependency requirements that must be met
